# Tally

A CFO for a fleet of coding agents. Give it a backlog and a budget. It sizes
each task, sends it to the cheapest model likely to finish it, stops any task
that overruns its spend ceiling, hands failed work to a stronger model, and
ends with a ledger tying every dollar to a merged PR.

Status: early build. The shared data contract exists, `tally demo` runs the
seven-task simulated demo backlog, and `tally run --dry-run` writes run state
plus a ledger from a file-backed backlog. The real AO worker path is wired and
ready for a gated one-task smoke run.

## Install

Prerequisites before you install:

- Node 20 or later.
- Agent Orchestrator installed and running.
- At least one signed-in coding agent that Agent Orchestrator can start.
- GitHub CLI installed and signed in with `gh auth login`.

Three ways in:

```bash
npm install -g github:Vaibhaav-Tiwari/neatlogs-hack
npm install -g tally-agents
git clone https://github.com/Vaibhaav-Tiwari/neatlogs-hack && cd neatlogs-hack && npm install && npm run build
```

The npm package is named `tally-agents`; the installed command is still
`tally`.

## Quickstart

Needs Node 20 or later.

```bash
npm install
npm run build
npm run tally -- demo --dashboard
npm run tally -- demo --live --dashboard
npm run tally -- dashboard
npm run tally -- doctor --config demo/tally.yaml
npm run tally -- run --dry-run --plan --config demo/tally.yaml
npm run tally -- login cfoai
npm run tally -- market --limit 5
```

The first two commands install and compile Tally. The remaining commands show
the full fake-worker demo, the read-only live-integration demo, the standalone
dashboard, integration checks, a dry-run plan, cfo.ai login, and the CrustData
market search. Run them one at a time; dashboard commands keep serving until
you stop them. Commands that call external services report the missing login or
API key instead of printing secrets. During development, `npm run tally --
<command>` runs the CLI from source. After `npm run build`,
`node bin/tally.js <command>` runs the compiled package entry.

For routine validation, run:

```bash
npm test
```

## Commands

| Command | What it will do |
|---|---|
| `tally run` | Run the backlog against the budget in `tally.yaml`. Flags: `--dry-run`, `--budget <usd>`, `--only <task>`, `--baseline`, `--config <path>`, `--plan`, `--dashboard`/`--open`. |
| `tally demo` | Run the full loop with simulated workers on `demo/tally.yaml` and `demo/sample-backlog.yaml`. No accounts or keys. Writes `.tally/runs/<run-id>/run.json` and `ledger.json`; add `--dashboard` for the one-command demo, or `--live` to light up read-only integrations while workers stay fake. |
| `tally dashboard` | Serve `dashboard/` and `.tally/runs/` read-only on `127.0.0.1`. The printed URL passes `?data=/runs/latest/` so the page reads the stable latest-run mirror. |
| `tally init` | Detect the test command, ask for a budget and issue label, and write `tally.yaml`. |
| `tally doctor` | One line per integration: connected, missing or broken, with the fix. |

## Layout

| Folder | Holds |
|---|---|
| `schema/` | The contract every part reads: TypeScript types, JSON Schema, validators, and a sample finished run in `schema/fixtures/finished-run/`. |
| `engine/` | The run loop, run state and ledger. |
| `adapters/` | One thin module per outside tool (Agent Orchestrator, Entire, neatlogs, cfo.ai, GitHub). |
| `agent/` | The CFO agent: sizing, routing, ceilings, escalation. |
| `cli/` | The `tally` command. |
| `dashboard/` | Static page that reads the ledger and run state. |
| `demo/` | Sample backlog and scripted outcomes for `tally demo`. |

## Configuration

With `integrations.entire: true`, enable Entire in the target repository and
trust its Codex hooks through `/hooks` before starting workers. Tally records
the task commit's `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer and its native `entireSessionId`
separately from the AO `sessionId`. Logs-only checkpoints retain conversation
context; escalation uses a generated summary when available and otherwise
describes the recorded files without claiming an AI summary was generated.
When Tally publishes a verified branch, it also pushes the checkpoint refs
named by its new commits to `origin` and to an `entire` remote when configured.
Checkpoint upload failures are reported as publishing failures. Dry runs do
not publish branches or checkpoints.

Entire documents commit links as
`https://entire.io/gh/<org>/<repo>/commit/<commit-sha>`. Tally keeps
`checkpointUrl` null unless the CLI returns a URL; a local checkpoint does not
by itself establish that a hosted link works.

Tally assumes nothing about the repository it works on. The repository, test
command, model tiers, list prices, ceilings and budget all come from
`tally.yaml` (a tier is a name, harness, model id, provider, list price and ceiling share); see `schema/fixtures/finished-run/tally.yaml` for a complete
example and `schema/tally-config.schema.json` for the rules.

Money in the ledger and run state is stored as integer nanos of USD
(1 USD = 1,000,000,000). Cost is always tokens multiplied by the list price in
`tally.yaml`.

For dry runs, set `backlog.source: file` and point `backlog.file` at YAML like:

```yaml
tasks:
  - id: T1
    title: Add validation for empty player name
    size: small
    outcomes: [passed]
  - id: T2
    title: Persist settings after restart
    size: medium
    outcomes: [stopped, passed]
```

`outcomes` is optional and defaults to one passed simulated attempt.

The latest run is also mirrored to `.tally/runs/latest/run.json` and
`.tally/runs/latest/ledger.json` so the dashboard has one stable path to poll.

## Secrets

Keys live in `~/.tally/.env`, outside every repository, and are loaded from
there. Never put them in this repo; `.env` files are git-ignored.


The npm package is named `tally-agents`; the installed command is still
`tally`.

## Quickstart

Needs Node 20 or later.

```bash
npm install
npm run build
npm run tally -- demo --dashboard
npm run tally -- demo --live --dashboard
npm run tally -- dashboard
npm run tally -- doctor --config demo/tally.yaml
npm run tally -- run --dry-run --plan --config demo/tally.yaml
npm run tally -- login cfoai
npm run tally -- market --limit 5
```

The first two commands install and compile Tally. The remaining commands show
the full fake-worker demo, the read-only live-integration demo, the standalone
dashboard, integration checks, a dry-run plan, cfo.ai login, and the CrustData
market search. Run them one at a time; dashboard commands keep serving until
you stop them. Commands that call external services report the missing login or
API key instead of printing secrets. During development, `npm run tally --
<command>` runs the CLI from source. After `npm run build`,
`node bin/tally.js <command>` runs the compiled package entry.

For routine validation, run:

```bash
npm test
```

## Commands

| Command | What it will do |
|---|---|
| `tally run` | Run the backlog against the budget in `tally.yaml`. Flags: `--dry-run`, `--budget <usd>`, `--only <task>`, `--baseline`, `--config <path>`, `--plan`, `--dashboard`/`--open`. |
| `tally demo` | Run the full loop with simulated workers on `demo/tally.yaml` and `demo/sample-backlog.yaml`. No accounts or keys. Writes `.tally/runs/<run-id>/run.json` and `ledger.json`; add `--dashboard` for the one-command demo, or `--live` to light up read-only integrations while workers stay fake. |
| `tally dashboard` | Serve `dashboard/` and `.tally/runs/` read-only on `127.0.0.1`. The printed URL passes `?data=/runs/latest/` so the page reads the stable latest-run mirror. |
| `tally init` | Detect the test command, ask for a budget and issue label, and write `tally.yaml`. |
| `tally doctor` | One line per integration: connected, missing or broken, with the fix. |

## Layout

| Folder | Holds |
|---|---|
| `schema/` | The contract every part reads: TypeScript types, JSON Schema, validators, and a sample finished run in `schema/fixtures/finished-run/`. |
| `engine/` | The run loop, run state and ledger. |
| `adapters/` | One thin module per outside tool (Agent Orchestrator, Entire, neatlogs, cfo.ai, GitHub). |
| `agent/` | The CFO agent: sizing, routing, ceilings, escalation. |
| `cli/` | The `tally` command. |
| `dashboard/` | Static page that reads the ledger and run state. |
| `demo/` | Sample backlog and scripted outcomes for `tally demo`. |

## Configuration

With `integrations.entire: true`, enable Entire in the target repository and
trust its Codex hooks through `/hooks` before starting workers. Tally records
the task commit's `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer and its native `entireSessionId`
separately from the AO `sessionId`. Logs-only checkpoints retain conversation
context; escalation uses a generated summary when available and otherwise
describes the recorded files without claiming an AI summary was generated.
When Tally publishes a verified branch, it also pushes the checkpoint refs
named by its new commits to `origin` and to an `entire` remote when configured.
Checkpoint upload failures are reported as publishing failures. Dry runs do
not publish branches or checkpoints.

Entire documents commit links as
`https://entire.io/gh/<org>/<repo>/commit/<commit-sha>`. Tally keeps
`checkpointUrl` null unless the CLI returns a URL; a local checkpoint does not
by itself establish that a hosted link works.

Tally assumes nothing about the repository it works on. The repository, test
command, model tiers, list prices, ceilings and budget all come from
`tally.yaml` (a tier is a name, harness, model id, provider, list price and ceiling share); see `schema/fixtures/finished-run/tally.yaml` for a complete
example and `schema/tally-config.schema.json` for the rules.

Money in the ledger and run state is stored as integer nanos of USD
(1 USD = 1,000,000,000). Cost is always tokens multiplied by the list price in
`tally.yaml`.

For dry runs, set `backlog.source: file` and point `backlog.file` at YAML like:

```yaml
tasks:
  - id: T1
    title: Add validation for empty player name
    size: small
    outcomes: [passed]
  - id: T2
    title: Persist settings after restart
    size: medium
    outcomes: [stopped, passed]
```

`outcomes` is optional and defaults to one passed simulated attempt.

The latest run is also mirrored to `.tally/runs/latest/run.json` and
`.tally/runs/latest/ledger.json` so the dashboard has one stable path to poll.

## Secrets

Keys live in `~/.tally/.env`, outside every repository, and are loaded from
there. Never put them in this repo; `.env` files are git-ignored.

item.stdout:
# Experiment summary: file and shape

Agreed between lane A (writes it, in `tally experiment`) and lane C (reads it, in the dashboard comparison view). Set by the orchestrator on 11 Oct.

## Where

- Each experiment gets a folder inside the runs directory: `.tally/runs/experiments/<experimentId>/summary.json`.
- The dashboard server already serves `.tally/runs` at `/runs/`, so the page reads `/runs/experiments/<experimentId>/summary.json`.
- `/runs/index.json` gains a second array, `experiments`: `[{ id, path: "/runs/experiments/<id>/", updatedAt, repo, real, status }]`, newest first.
- The individual run folders stay where they are (`/runs/<runId>/`), each with `mode` and `repeat` in `run.json`, so the per-run fallback keeps working.
- The summary is rewritten after every finished run, so the page can show an experiment in progress (`status: "running"`).

The comparison view reads the agreed experiment summary from the experiments entries in runs/index.json (or an explicit `?experiment=.../summary.json`). It refreshes summaries every poll, selects a matching repository/task set/real-or-simulated kind, and shows experiment status, budget, named repeats, progress and min/median/max statistics. Multiple compatible experiments can be selected.

The metric is labelled cost per passed task, matching lane A's summary contract; it does not imply a merged PR. Losses remain visible. If no compatible valid summary is available, the existing per-run comparison remains, with mode/repeat labels and statistics over finished runs only. Replay uses the per-run view.

Includes a contract fixture with two repeats per mode where Tally loses, and five focused tests. Rendered and inspected at 1440px and 390px in isolated headless Chrome. Browser checks exercised live waiting/stopped updates and incompatible-summary fallback, with zero app page errors; phone metrics fit x10..380 without horizontal scrolling. AO Browser still returns BROWSER_TARGET_MISMATCH. Full suite, build and typecheck pass. Publish import-completeness tests cover the new module through pattern-based asset copying.

Lane A's real experiment writer is still in progress; this implementation follows the agreed experiment-summary-spec.md contract.

item.stdout:
# Tally

Export a static dashboard snapshot with `tally publish --out site`, or choose
recorded folders with `tally publish --out site --runs run-id-1,run-id-2`.
The default includes real runs only. The command reads `.tally/runs`, scans
the exported files for sensitive content, and prints their sizes. Serve the
output directory on a static HTTP host, including under a sub-path. This
creates local files; it does not deploy them.

A CFO for a fleet of coding agents. Give it a backlog and a budget. It sizes
each task, sends it to the cheapest model likely to finish it, stops any task
that overruns its spend ceiling, hands failed work to a stronger model, and
ends with a ledger tying every dollar to a merged PR.

Status: early build, available from GitHub. The npm package `tally-agents`
has not been released yet. The seven-task demo uses simulated workers; real
runs use Agent Orchestrator and record their attempts and evidence separately.

## Install

Prerequisites before you install:

- Node 20 or later and npm.
- For real runs: Agent Orchestrator installed and running, with at least one
  signed-in coding agent it can start.
- For real runs: GitHub CLI installed and signed in with `gh auth login`.

The simulated demo and dashboard need only Node and npm. They do not need an
AO account, coding-agent login or GitHub credentials.

Three ways in:

1. **GitHub (available now):** `npm install -g github:Vaibhaav-Tiwari/neatlogs-hack`.
   Installation builds the CLI automatically.
2. **npm (not released yet):** after release, `npm install -g tally-agents`.
3. **Source checkout:** clone this repository, enter it, and run `npm install`.
   Then use `node bin/tally.js` in place of `tally` in the commands below.
   `npm install` builds the CLI through its prepare script.

The npm package is named `tally-agents`; the installed command is still
`tally`.

## Quickstart

After either global installation, start in an empty directory:

```bash
tally demo
tally dashboard
```

The demo writes `.tally/runs/` in that directory. Open the URL printed by
`tally dashboard`; it reads the latest run and lists recorded runs. Keep it
running while viewing the page, and press Ctrl-C to stop it. If its default
port is occupied, use `tally dashboard --port 0` for a free port.

`tally demo --live` keeps workers simulated while checking the configured
read-only integrations. Bundled cfo.ai workspace/table values are placeholders;
missing credentials are reported, and no real worker is launched.

### A Provided Tarball

With only a packed `tally-agents-0.1.0.tgz` in your current directory, these
commands install into a temporary prefix without changing your normal global
installation, then follow the same quickstart:

```bash
npm install -g --prefix "$PWD/tally-install" ./tally-agents-0.1.0.tgz
export PATH="$PWD/tally-install/bin:$PATH"
tally demo
tally dashboard --port 0
```

No checkout, manual build or `tally init` is needed for the demo.

### Your Repository

Run `tally init` from the repository you want Tally to work on only when you
consent to creating `tally.yaml` and an install record in `.tally/`, and to
registering/updating its AO project and setup hook. It asks for budget and
issue label; neatlogs, Entire and cfo.ai are separate opt-in prompts, defaulting
to No. The current build has no final review/confirmation prompt before those
configuration writes. Review the generated model tiers, prices, tests and
ceilings before starting workers.

Use `tally doctor`, then `tally run --plan` to inspect routing without spawning
workers. A real `tally run` starts workers and can publish verified branches
and pull requests. `tally run --dry-run` uses simulated workers instead.

`tally uninstall` lists the files and AO settings it owns and asks for
confirmation before removing them. It refuses to overwrite edits made since
init. It leaves run history, credentials and the globally installed CLI in
place; remove that CLI separately with `npm uninstall -g tally-agents`.

### Static Snapshot

`tally publish --out site` is implemented in PR #49 and is not on main or an
npm release yet. Once merged, it writes a self-contained static dashboard,
defaulting to real recorded runs. Select folders explicitly with
`tally publish --out site --runs run-id-1,run-id-2`; use this for simulated demo
data. It scans exported files for sensitive content and prints file sizes and
the total. Serve the directory on a static HTTP host, including under a
sub-path. This creates local files and does not deploy them.

During development, `npm run tally -- <command>` runs the CLI from source.

For routine validation, run:

```bash
npm test
```

## Commands

| Command | What it will do |
|---|---|
| `tally run` | Run the backlog against the budget in `tally.yaml`. Flags: `--dry-run`, `--budget <usd>`, `--only <task>`, `--baseline`, `--config <path>`, `--plan`, `--dashboard`/`--open`. |

each task, sends it to the cheapest model likely to finish it, stops any task
that overruns its spend ceiling, hands failed work to a stronger model, and
ends with a ledger tying every dollar to a merged PR.

{"chunk_id":"ea4d2d","wall_time_seconds":0.000004792,"exit_code":0,"original_token_count":723,"output":"# Experiment summary: file and shape

Agreed between lane A (writes it, in `tally experiment`) and lane C (reads it, in the dashboard comparison view). Set by the orchestrator on 11 Oct.

## Where

- Each experiment gets a folder inside the runs directory: `.tally/runs/experiments/<experimentId>/summary.json`.
- The dashboard server already serves `.tally/runs` at `/runs/`, so the page reads `/runs/experiments/<experimentId>/summary.json`.
- `/runs/index.json` gains a second array, `experiments`: `[{ id, path: "/runs/experiments/<id>/", updatedAt, repo, real, status }]`, newest first.
- The individual run folders stay where they are (`/runs/<runId>/`), each with `mode` and `repeat` in `run.json`, so the per-run fallback keeps working.
- The summary is rewritten after every finished run, so the page can show an experiment in progress (`status: "running"`).

## Shape

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "experimentId": "exp-20261011-020000Z",
  "status": "running | finished | stopped",
  "real": true,
  "repo": "Vaibhaav-Tiwari/fly-doom-jev",
  "baseCommit": "565e6ccd757ff794ead643dac7359efe67ec9db2",
  "taskIds": ["FDJ-1", "FDJ-2"],
  "repeatsPlanned": 2,
  "startedAt": "ISO time",
  "endedAt": "ISO time or null",
  "budget": { "capNanos": 0, "spentNanos": 0 },
  "modes": {
    "baseline": {
      "runs": [
        { "runId": "run-...", "repeat": 1, "path": "/runs/run-.../", "status": "finished",
          "tasks": 7, "passed": 6, "failed": 1, "skipped": 0, "attempts": 7,
          "totalCostNanos": 0, "costPerPassedTaskNanos": 0, "passRate": 0.86,
          "neatlogsSessionId": "string or null" }
      ],
      "totalCostNanos": { "min": 0, "median": 0, "max": 0 },
      "costPerPassedTaskNanos": { "min": 0, "median": 0, "max": 0 },
      "passRate": { "min": 0, "median": 0, "max": 0 }
    },
    "tally": { "same shape as baseline": true }
  },
  "perTask": [
    { "taskId": "FDJ-1",
      "baseline": [ { "runId": "run-...", "repeat": 1, "tier": "top", "model": "string", "result": "passed", "attempts": 1, "costNanos": 0 } ],
      "tally":    [ { "runId": "run-...", "repeat": 1, "tier": "cheap", "model": "string", "result": "passed", "attempts": 2, "costNanos": 0 } ] }
  ],
  "comparison": {
    "totalCostChangePct": -42.0,
    "costPerPassedTaskChangePct": -40.0,
    "passRateChangePoints": -5.0,
    "note": "medians of the repeats; negative cost change means Tally was cheaper"
  }
}
```

Rules:

- Money is in nanos of USD, as everywhere else in Tally.
- `comparison` values are `null` until both modes have at least one finished run.
- With one repeat, `min`, `median` and `max` are equal; the page then shows a single value, not a range.
- Nothing is rounded or dropped to make Tally look better. A run where Tally loses appears like any other.
- Cost per passed task is total cost of the run divided by passed tasks, and `null` when none passed.
"}

{"chunk_id":"5f28be","wall_time_seconds":0.000006708,"exit_code":0,"original_token_count":1611,"output":"# Tally

Export a static dashboard snapshot with `tally publish --out site`, or choose
recorded folders with `tally publish --out site --runs run-id-1,run-id-2`.
The default includes real runs only. The command reads `.tally/runs`, scans
the exported files for sensitive content, and prints their sizes. Serve the
output directory on a static HTTP host, including under a sub-path. This
creates local files; it does not deploy them.

A CFO for a fleet of coding agents. Give it a backlog and a budget. It sizes
each task, sends it to the cheapest model likely to finish it, stops any task
that overruns its spend ceiling, hands failed work to a stronger model, and
ends with a ledger tying every dollar to a merged PR.

Status: early build, available from GitHub. The npm package `tally-agents`
has not been released yet. The seven-task demo uses simulated workers; real
runs use Agent Orchestrator and record their attempts and evidence separately.

## Install

Prerequisites before you install:

- Node 20 or later and npm.
- For real runs: Agent Orchestrator installed and running, with at least one
  signed-in coding agent it can start.
- For real runs: GitHub CLI installed and signed in with `gh auth login`.

The simulated demo and dashboard need only Node and npm. They do not need an
AO account, coding-agent login or GitHub credentials.

Three ways in:

1. **GitHub (available now):** `npm install -g github:Vaibhaav-Tiwari/neatlogs-hack`.
   Installation builds the CLI automatically.
2. **npm (not released yet):** after release, `npm install -g tally-agents`.
3. **Source checkout:** clone this repository, enter it, and run `npm install`.
   Then use `node bin/tally.js` in place of `tally` in the commands below.
   `npm install` builds the CLI through its prepare script.

The npm package is named `tally-agents`; the installed command is still
`tally`.

## Quickstart

After either global installation, start in an empty directory:

```bash
tally demo
tally dashboard
```

The demo writes `.tally/runs/` in that directory. Open the URL printed by
`tally dashboard`; it reads the latest run and lists recorded runs. Keep it
running while viewing the page, and press Ctrl-C to stop it. If its default
port is occupied, use `tally dashboard --port 0` for a free port.

`tally demo --live` keeps workers simulated while checking the configured
read-only integrations. Bundled cfo.ai workspace/table values are placeholders;
missing credentials are reported, and no real worker is launched.

### A Provided Tarball

With only a packed `tally-agents-0.1.0.tgz` in your current directory, these
commands install into a temporary prefix without changing your normal global
installation, then follow the same quickstart:

```bash
npm install -g --prefix "$PWD/tally-install" ./tally-agents-0.1.0.tgz
export PATH="$PWD/tally-install/bin:$PATH"
tally demo
tally dashboard --port 0
```

No checkout, manual build or `tally init` is needed for the demo.

### Your Repository

Run `tally init` from the repository you want Tally to work on only when you
consent to creating `tally.yaml` and an install record in `.tally/`, and to
registering/updating its AO project and setup hook. It asks for budget and
issue label; neatlogs, Entire and cfo.ai are separate opt-in prompts, defaulting
to No. The current build has no final review/confirmation prompt before those
configuration writes. Review the generated model tiers, prices, tests and
ceilings before starting workers.

Use `tally doctor`, then `tally run --plan` to inspect routing without spawning
workers. A real `tally run` starts workers and can publish verified branches
and pull requests. `tally run --dry-run` uses simulated workers instead.

`tally uninstall` lists the files and AO settings it owns and asks for
confirmation before removing them. It refuses to overwrite edits made since
init. It leaves run history, credentials and the globally installed CLI in
place; remove that CLI separately with `npm uninstall -g tally-agents`.

### Static Snapshot

`tally publish --out site` is implemented in PR #49 and is not on main or an
npm release yet. Once merged, it writes a self-contained static dashboard,
defaulting to real recorded runs. Select folders explicitly with
`tally publish --out site --runs run-id-1,run-id-2`; use this for simulated demo
data. It scans exported files for sensitive content and prints file sizes and
the total. Serve the directory on a static HTTP host, including under a
sub-path. This creates local files and does not deploy them.

During development, `npm run tally -- <command>` runs the CLI from source.

For routine validation, run:

```bash
npm test
```

|---|---|

---
name: using-ao
description: "Catalog of the AO (Agent Orchestrator) `ao` CLI: spawning workers, managing sessions and projects, creating reusable Cues, sending messages, controlling the shared browser, previewing pages, and daemon control. Use when using the ao CLI, creating Cues, spawning workers, or managing AO sessions in an AO workspace."
trigger: "Using the ao CLI in an AO workspace: creating Cues, spawning workers, managing sessions/projects, sending messages, controlling or previewing pages."
---

# AO CLI Catalog

`ao` is a thin CLI over the local AO daemon. Every command is `ao <command> --help` for the authoritative flag list.

| Command | What it does | When to use | Details |
|---|---|---|---|
| `spawn` | Spawn a project worker, orchestrator, or projectless standalone worker | Starting a new task or issue | [commands/spawn.md](commands/spawn.md) |
| `session` | Manage agent sessions (list, kill, rename, restore, etc.) | Inspecting or controlling running/terminated sessions | [commands/session.md](commands/session.md) |
| `agent` | Inspect installed harnesses and launch readiness | Choosing or diagnosing an agent harness | `ao agent ls --refresh` |
| `pr` | Merge a PR or resolve its review threads | Completing a reviewed change | `ao pr merge` / `ao pr resolve-comments` |
| `project` | Register, inspect, configure, or remove projects | Setting up or managing repos AO knows about | [commands/project.md](commands/project.md) |
| `automation` | Manage durable recurring session automations | Creating, editing, disabling, deleting, and inspecting scheduled runs | [commands/automation.md](commands/automation.md) |
| `cue` | Create or list reusable project Cues | Saving a repetitive command or agent task at the user's request | [commands/cue.md](commands/cue.md) |
| `orchestrator` | List orchestrator sessions | Viewing which sessions are orchestrators | [commands/orchestrator.md](commands/orchestrator.md) |
| `review` | Start, list, cancel, or submit AO's native reviewer for a worker's PR (default: this session) | Getting an adversarial review of an AO session's PR; never spawn a worker to review | [commands/review.md](commands/review.md) |
| `send` | Send a message to a running agent session | Correcting or directing a live agent | [commands/send.md](commands/send.md) |
| `report` | Persist a meaningful worker report | Checkpoints, blockers, decisions, outputs, and completion | [commands/report.md](commands/report.md) |
| `preview` | Start a session-owned app or open an exact URL/file | Running and showing the worker's relevant app, Markdown, HTML, PDF, or image | [commands/preview.md](commands/preview.md) |
| `render` | Show a self-contained HTML page inline in a chat thread | Answering with a chart, table, diagram, or mockup | [commands/render.md](commands/render.md) |
| `browser` | Inspect and control the session's shared live browser | Verifying a web app through snapshots, interactions, waits, screenshots, console, and errors | [commands/browser.md](commands/browser.md) |
| `start` | Fetch (if needed) and open the AO desktop app | Launching the app | [commands/start.md](commands/start.md) |
| `stop` | Stop the AO daemon | Shutting down AO | [commands/stop.md](commands/stop.md) |
| `status` | Show daemon status | Verifying the daemon is up and healthy | [commands/status.md](commands/status.md) |
| `doctor` | Run local health checks | Diagnosing AO setup problems | [commands/doctor.md](commands/doctor.md) |
| `import` | Import projects from a legacy AO install | Migrating from the old flat-file store | [commands/import.md](commands/import.md) |
| `version` | Print version information | Checking installed version | - |
| `completion` | Generate shell completion scripts | Setting up tab completion | - |

## Conventions

- Most read commands accept `--json` for machine-readable output.
- `-p / --project` scopes session subcommand lookups to one project.
- Session and project ids are shown by `ao session ls` and `ao project ls`.
- To refer to a session in AO Chat or the AO terminal, use the canonical in-app
  link `ao://sessions/{project-id}/{session-id}`. Read
  [commands/session.md](commands/session.md) for identity, encoding, and safety
  rules before constructing one.
- When the user asks to save a repeatable task as a Cue, use `ao cue list --json` to check existing definitions, then `ao cue create`. An agent Cue stores a reusable instruction; a command Cue stores an exact shell command. This agent-facing command can create and read Cues, but cannot edit or delete them. Direct the user to project settings for changes to existing Cues.
- `--agent` is an alias for `--harness` on `ao spawn`.
- Every command accepts `-h / --help` for the full flag list.
- For frontend launch, preview selection, or artifact handoff, read
  [commands/preview.md](commands/preview.md) before acting. Its static-file,
  project-runtime, and automatic-handoff rules are load-bearing.
- For page inspection, interaction, or request diagnosis, read
  [commands/browser.md](commands/browser.md). It defines shared-tab behavior
  and the opt-in network policy.

Use [references.md](references.md) only when a natural-language request does
not map clearly to a command above.

# Tally

A CFO for a fleet of coding agents. Give it a backlog and a budget. It sizes
each task, sends it to the cheapest model likely to finish it, stops any task
that overruns its spend ceiling, hands failed work to a stronger model, and
ends with a ledger tying every dollar to a merged PR.

Status: early build, available from GitHub. The npm package `tally-agents`
has not been released yet. The seven-task demo uses simulated workers; real
runs use Agent Orchestrator and record their attempts and evidence separately.

## Install

Prerequisites before you install:

- Node 20 or later and npm.
- For real runs: Agent Orchestrator installed and running, with at least one
  signed-in coding agent it can start.
- For real runs: GitHub CLI installed and signed in with `gh auth login`.

The simulated demo and dashboard need only Node and npm. They do not need an
AO account, coding-agent login or GitHub credentials.

Three ways in:

1. **GitHub (available now):** `npm install -g github:Vaibhaav-Tiwari/neatlogs-hack`.
   Installation builds the CLI automatically.
2. **npm (not released yet):** after release, `npm install -g tally-agents`.
3. **Source checkout:** `git clone https://github.com/Vaibhaav-Tiwari/neatlogs-hack`,
   enter `neatlogs-hack`, and run `npm install`.
   Then use `node bin/tally.js` in place of `tally` in the commands below.
   `npm install` builds the CLI through its prepare script.

The npm package is named `tally-agents`; the installed command is still
`tally`.

## Quickstart

After either global installation, start in an empty directory:

```bash
tally demo
tally dashboard
```

The demo writes `.tally/runs/` in that directory. Open the URL printed by
`tally dashboard`; it reads the latest run and lists recorded runs. Keep it
running while viewing the page, and press Ctrl-C to stop it. If its default
port is occupied, use `tally dashboard --port 0` for a free port.

`tally demo --live` keeps workers simulated while checking the configured
read-only integrations. Bundled cfo.ai workspace/table values are placeholders;
missing credentials are reported, and no real worker is launched.

### A Provided Tarball

With only a packed `tally-agents-0.1.0.tgz` in your current directory, these
commands install into a temporary prefix without changing your normal global
installation, then follow the same quickstart:

```bash
npm install -g --prefix "$PWD/tally-install" ./tally-agents-0.1.0.tgz
export PATH="$PWD/tally-install/bin:$PATH"
tally demo
tally dashboard --port 0
```

No checkout, manual build or `tally init` is needed for the demo.

### Your Repository

Run `tally init` from the repository you want Tally to work on. It asks for
budget and issue label; neatlogs, Entire and cfo.ai are separate opt-in prompts,
defaulting to No. It displays the proposed `tally.yaml`, install record in
`.tally/`, AO project registration/configuration and setup hook, then asks for
final confirmation (default No) before applying changes. Use `tally init
--dry-run` to preview without applying, or `--yes` only when you consent to
applying detected defaults without prompts. Review model tiers, prices, tests
and ceilings before starting workers. Scoped worker allow-list enforcement is
not yet installed; init does not change global coding-agent settings.

Use `tally doctor`, then `tally run --plan` to inspect routing without spawning
workers. A real `tally run` starts workers and can publish verified branches
and pull requests. `tally run --dry-run` uses simulated workers instead.

`tally uninstall` lists the files and AO settings it owns and asks for
confirmation before removing them. It refuses to overwrite edits made since
init. It leaves run history, credentials and the globally installed CLI in
place; remove that CLI separately with `npm uninstall -g tally-agents`.

### Static Snapshot

`tally publish --out site` writes a self-contained static dashboard,
defaulting to real recorded runs. Select folders explicitly with
`tally publish --out site --runs run-id-1,run-id-2`; use this for simulated demo
data. It scans exported files for sensitive content and prints file sizes and
the total. Serve the directory on a static HTTP host, including under a
sub-path. This creates local files and does not deploy them.

During development, `npm run tally -- <command>` runs the CLI from source.

For routine validation, run:

```bash
npm test
```

## Commands

| Command | What it will do |
|---|---|
| `tally run` | Run the backlog against the budget in `tally.yaml`. Flags: `--dry-run`, `--budget <usd>`, `--only <task>`, `--baseline`, `--config <path>`, `--plan`, `--dashboard`/`--open`. |
| `tally demo` | Run the full loop with simulated workers on `demo/tally.yaml` and `demo/sample-backlog.yaml`. No accounts or keys. Writes `.tally/runs/<run-id>/run.json` and `ledger.json`; add `--dashboard` for the one-command demo, or `--live` to light up read-only integrations while workers stay fake. |
| `tally dashboard` | Serve `dashboard/` and `.tally/runs/` read-only on `127.0.0.1`. The printed URL passes `?data=/runs/latest/` so the page reads the stable latest-run mirror. |
| `tally init` | Preview files and AO changes, then ask final default-No consent. `--dry-run` previews; `--yes` applies defaults without prompts. Scoped worker allow-list enforcement is not yet installed. |
| `tally uninstall` | Confirm removal of init-owned configuration and AO settings; preserve history and credentials. |
| `tally doctor` | One line per integration: connected, missing or broken, with the fix. |
| `tally login cfoai` | Sign in to cfo.ai; tokens are cached outside the repository. |
| `tally market --limit 5` | Search CrustData for companies adopting coding agents; requires its credentials. |
| `tally publish --out site` | Static dashboard export with a sensitive-content scan. No deployment. |

## Layout

| Folder | Holds |
|---|---|
| `schema/` | The contract every part reads: TypeScript types, JSON Schema, validators, and a sample finished run in `schema/fixtures/finished-run/`. |
| `engine/` | The run loop, run state and ledger. |
| `adapters/` | One thin module per outside tool (Agent Orchestrator, Entire, neatlogs, cfo.ai, GitHub). |
| `agent/` | The CFO agent: sizing, routing, ceilings, escalation. |
| `cli/` | The `tally` command. |
| `dashboard/` | Static page that reads the ledger and run state. |
| `demo/` | Sample backlog and scripted outcomes for `tally demo`. |

## Configuration

With `integrations.entire: true`, enable Entire in the target repository and
trust its Codex hooks through `/hooks` before starting workers. Tally records
the task commit's `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer and its native `entireSessionId`
separately from the AO `sessionId`. Logs-only checkpoints retain conversation
context; escalation defaults to a metadata-only handoff containing the
checkpoint/session IDs, branch, recorded and changed files, attempt verdict,
and task text. It does not generate a summary or export a transcript.
`entire.generatedSummaries: true` explicitly opts into Entire's summary
provider (`checkpoint explain --generate`), which may export session content;
this setting is off by default and requires the user's approval.
When Tally publishes a verified branch, it also pushes the checkpoint refs
named by its new commits to `origin` and to an `entire` remote when configured.
Checkpoint upload failures are reported as publishing failures. Dry runs do
not publish branches or checkpoints.

Entire documents commit links as
`https://entire.io/gh/<org>/<repo>/commit/<commit-sha>`. Tally keeps
`checkpointUrl` null unless the CLI returns a URL; a local checkpoint does not
by itself establish that a hosted link works.

Tally assumes nothing about the repository it works on. The repository, test
command, model tiers, list prices, ceilings and budget all come from
`tally.yaml` (a tier is a name, harness, model id, provider, list price and ceiling share); see `schema/fixtures/finished-run/tally.yaml` for a complete
example and `schema/tally-config.schema.json` for the rules.

Money in the ledger and run state is stored as integer nanos of USD
(1 USD = 1,000,000,000). Cost is always tokens multiplied by the list price in
`tally.yaml`.

For dry runs, set `backlog.source: file` and point `backlog.file` at YAML like:

```yaml
tasks:
  - id: T1
    title: Add validation for empty player name
    size: small
    outcomes: [passed]
  - id: T2
    title: Persist settings after restart
    size: medium
    outcomes: [stopped, passed]
```

`outcomes` is optional and defaults to one passed simulated attempt.

// Tally dashboard. Reads run.json and ledger.json on a timer and redraws.
// It never writes anything.

import { frameAt } from './replay-core.js';
import { displayedCost, isRunning, withLiveCosts } from './live-state.js';

const NANOS_PER_USD = 1_000_000_000;

const query = new URLSearchParams(location.search);
const defaults = window.TALLY_DASHBOARD ?? {};
const asFolder = (path) => (path.endsWith('/') ? path : `${path}/`);
const hasExplicitData = query.has('data');
const wantsDemo = query.has('demo');
const wantsReplay = query.has('replay');
const config = {
  data: asFolder(query.get('data') ?? defaults.data ?? './'),
  runsIndex: query.get('runsIndex') ?? defaults.runsIndex ?? '/runs/index.json',
  baseline: query.get('baseline') ?? defaults.baseline ?? null,
  intervalMs: Math.max(250, Number(query.get('interval') ?? defaults.intervalMs ?? 2000) || 2000),
  aoProject: query.get('aoProject') ?? defaults.aoProject ?? null,
  liveCeilingSec: Math.max(30, Number(query.get('liveCeilingSec') ?? defaults.liveCeilingSec ?? 180) || 180),
  sample: defaults.sample ?? null,
  // ?demo shows the checked-in sample. ?replay=60 plays the chosen run over that many seconds.
  useSample: wantsDemo || (wantsReplay && !hasExplicitData),
  replaySec: wantsReplay ? Math.max(5, Number(query.get('replay')) || 60) : null,
# ao report

Persist a meaningful worker report for durable delivery to the active project
orchestrator.

## Syntax

```text
ao report <free-form-text>
ao report --checkpoint --note <text> [output flags]
ao report --needs-input --note <text> [output flags]
ao report --stuck --note <text> [output flags]
ao report --done --note <text> [output flags]
```

Output flags are repeatable:

```text
--artifact <opaque-reference>
--pr-created <pr-or-mr-url>
--pr-reviewed <pr-or-mr-url>
```

Use reports for meaningful transitions, decisions, blockers, required input,
outputs, and terminal judgment. Do not narrate routine commands. Outputs do not
imply completion, and `--done` does not terminate the session.

# ao session

Manage agent sessions: list, inspect, rename, kill, restore, exit or resume an
agent, switch harnesses, clean up, and claim PRs.

## In-app session links

When referring a user or another agent to a session in AO Chat or the AO
terminal, emit this canonical link:

```text
ao://sessions/{project-id}/{session-id}
```

- Use stable IDs returned by `ao project ls` and `ao session ls`, or the current
  session's `AO_PROJECT_ID` and `AO_SESSION_ID`. Never use display names as
  identity; renaming a session must not change its link.
- Treat the project ID and session ID as separate URL path segments. Encode
  either ID with URL percent encoding if it contains characters that are not
  safe in one segment.
- Emit only the navigation route above. Do not append query strings, fragments,
  action names, credentials, authorities, or extra path segments.
- The link is handled only inside a currently running AO desktop app. It is not
  an operating-system protocol link and must not be described as supporting
  cold launch or navigation from external applications.
- A session link navigates; it never sends a message, executes a command, or
  performs another action.

Example for project `mercury` and session `mer-3`:

```text
ao://sessions/mercury/mer-3
```

## Syntax

```
ao session <subcommand> [args] [flags]
```

## Subcommands

---

### ao session ls

List sessions.

**Syntax:**
```
ao session ls [flags]
```

**Flags:**

| Flag | Meaning | Default / Required |
|---|---|---|
| `-a, --all` | Include orchestrator sessions | - |
| `--include-terminated` | Include terminated sessions | - |
| `--json` | Output as JSON | - |
| `-p, --project string` | Filter by project ID | - |

**Examples:**

```bash
# List all active worker sessions
ao session ls
```

```bash
# List all sessions including terminated, scoped to one project
ao session ls --include-terminated -p agent-orchestrator
```

---

### ao session get

Fetch one session.

**Syntax:**
```
ao session get <id> [flags]
```

**Flags:**

| Flag | Meaning | Default / Required |
|---|---|---|
| `--json` | Output as JSON | - |
| `-p, --project string` | Project id to scope the lookup | - |

**Examples:**

```bash
# Get details for session mer-3
ao session get mer-3
```

```bash
# Get session details as JSON
ao session get mer-3 --json
```

---

### ao session kill

Terminate a session.

**Syntax:**
```
ao session kill <id> [flags]
```

**Flags:**

| Flag | Meaning | Default / Required |
|---|---|---|
| `-p, --project string` | Project id to scope the lookup | - |

**Examples:**

```bash
# Kill session mer-3
ao session kill mer-3
```

---

### ao session rename

Rename a worker session. The project orchestrator cannot be renamed, including by itself; the daemon refuses with `ORCHESTRATOR_RENAME_UNSUPPORTED`.

**Syntax:**
```
ao session rename <id> <name> [flags]
```

**Flags:**

| Flag | Meaning | Default / Required |
|---|---|---|
| `-p, --project string` | Project id to scope the lookup | - |

**Examples:**

```bash
# Rename session mer-3 to a new display name
ao session rename mer-3 "fix-auth-bug"
```

---

### ao session restore

Restore a terminated session or resume an exited agent.

**Syntax:**
```
ao session restore <id> [flags]
```

**Flags:**

| Flag | Meaning | Default / Required |
|---|---|---|
| `-p, --project string` | Project id to scope the lookup | - |

**Examples:**

```bash
# Restore a terminated session
ao session restore mer-3
```

---

### ao session exit-agent

Exit an agent without terminating its AO session. The session can later be
resumed in place.

**Syntax:**
```
ao session exit-agent <id> [flags]
```

**Flags:**

| Flag | Meaning | Default / Required |
|---|---|---|
| `--json` | Output as JSON | - |
| `-p, --project string` | Project id to scope the lookup | - |

---

### ao session resume-agent

Resume an exited agent in its existing AO session.

**Syntax:**
```
ao session resume-agent <id> [flags]
```

**Flags:**

| Flag | Meaning | Default / Required |
|---|---|---|
| `--json` | Output as JSON | - |
| `-p, --project string` | Project id to scope the lookup | - |

**Examples:**

```bash
ao session exit-agent mer-3
ao session resume-agent mer-3
```

---

### ao session switch-agent

Switch a running session to another installed agent harness. This preserves the
AO session while provisioning the target harness.

**Syntax:**
```
ao session switch-agent <id> <target-harness> [flags]
```

**Flags:**

| Flag | Meaning | Default / Required |
|---|---|---|
| `--idempotency-key string` | Reuse a prior identical switch request safely | - |
| `--json` | Output the agent switch as JSON | - |

**Examples:**

```bash
ao session switch-agent mer-3 codex
```

---

### ao session agent-switch ls

List agent-harness switches recorded for a session. Alias: `agent-switches`.

**Syntax:**
```
ao session agent-switch ls <session-id> [flags]
```

**Flags:**

| Flag | Meaning | Default / Required |
|---|---|---|
| `--json` | Output agent switches as JSON | - |

**Examples:**

```bash
ao session agent-switch ls mer-3
```

---

### ao session cleanup

Clean up terminated sessions by reclaiming eligible workspaces. Dirty worktrees are skipped by the daemon.

**Syntax:**
```
ao session cleanup [flags]
```

**Flags:**

| Flag | Meaning | Default / Required |
|---|---|---|
| `--dry-run` | Preview which sessions would be cleaned without removing anything | - |
| `-p, --project string` | Filter by project ID | - |
| `-y, --yes` | Skip confirmation prompt | - |

**Examples:**

```bash
# Clean up all terminated sessions (skip prompt)
ao session cleanup -y
```

```bash
# Clean up terminated sessions for one project
ao session cleanup -p agent-orchestrator
```

```bash
# Preview eligible cleanup candidates
ao session cleanup --dry-run
```

---

### ao session claim-pr

Attach an existing PR to the current AO session, or target another session explicitly.

**Syntax:**
```
ao session claim-pr <pr-ref> [flags]
ao session claim-pr <session-id> <pr-ref> [flags]
```

With one positional argument, `AO_SESSION_ID` supplies the session. This is the preferred form inside a worker. Pass both arguments from an orchestrator or external shell when targeting another session.

**Flags:**

| Flag | Meaning | Default / Required |
|---|---|---|
| `--json` | Output as JSON | - |
| `--no-takeover` | Refuse if another active session owns the PR | - |
| `-p, --project string` | Project id to scope the lookup | - |

**Examples:**

```bash
# Attach PR 88 to the current worker session
ao session claim-pr 88
```

```bash
# Attach PR 88 to session mer-3 explicitly
ao session claim-pr mer-3 88
```

```bash
# Claim PR 88 for the current worker but refuse if another session owns it
ao session claim-pr 88 --no-takeover
```
# ao send

Send a message to a running agent session. Use this to correct or direct a live agent mid-stream without killing and respawning it.

## Syntax

```
ao send [flags]
```

## Flags

| Flag | Meaning | Default / Required |
|---|---|---|
| `--message string` | Message body | Required unless `--recover-only` |
| `--session string` | Session id | Required |
| `--steer` | Add guidance to the active Chat turn, or start a normal turn when idle | Optional |
| `--client-message-id string` | Stable delivery handle for steering and safe retries | Generated automatically with `--steer` |
| `--recover-only` | Recover the outcome for an existing delivery handle without resending | Requires `--steer` and `--client-message-id` |

## Steering and recovery

`--steer` uses one atomic daemon operation. If the session has an active Chat
turn, the message is added to that turn. If the session is idle, the message
starts a normal Chat turn. The state cannot change between those decisions and
leave the message queued as a separate correction.

Every steering request has a client message id. Supply one explicitly when a
caller must retain the handle across retries:

```bash
ao send --session mer-3 --steer --client-message-id correction-42 --message "Focus only on the backend."
```

If the command reports an uncertain outcome or a transport failure, preserve
the delivery handle printed in the error. Recover the existing result without
contacting the provider again:

```bash
ao send --session mer-3 --steer --recover-only --client-message-id correction-42
```

Do not invent a new client message id after an uncertain result. Reusing the
original id lets the daemon return the durable steering receipt or normal turn
without delivering the message twice. Recovery confirms the recorded delivery
outcome, not that the agent acted on the guidance.

## Examples

```bash
# Send a correction to a running session
ao send --session mer-3 --message "Focus only on the backend; ignore frontend files."
```

```bash
# Give the agent new instructions mid-task
ao send --session mer-3 --message "The issue is in session_manager.go line 142, not in the CLI. Investigate there."
```

```bash
# Steer the active Chat turn, or start a normal turn if it is idle
ao send --session mer-3 --steer --message "Use the daemon DTO as the source of truth."
```
import { basename } from 'node:path';
import { costNanos } from '../schema/money.js';
import type { TallyConfig, TaskSize, Tier, TokenUsage } from '../schema/types.js';
import { PriceHistory } from '../agent/history.js';
import type { HandoffSummary, LiveUsage, LiveUsagePort, SessionControlPort, SizingSignals, SizingSignalsPort } from '../agent/ports.js';
import type { VerifierPort, VerifyInput, VerifyResult } from '../adapters/verifier.js';
import { type BacklogTask, loadFileBacklog, type ScriptedAttempt } from './backlog.js';
import type { RealRunPorts, WorkerPort, WorkerResult, WorkerStartInput } from './real.js';

interface DrySession {
  sessionId: string;
  task: BacklogTask;
  attempt: number;
  tier: Tier;
  ceilingNanos: number | null;
  script: ScriptedAttempt;
  branch: string;
  checkoutPath: string;
  stopped: boolean;
  resolve?: (result: WorkerResult) => void;
}

class DryRunState implements WorkerPort, LiveUsagePort, SessionControlPort, VerifierPort {
  private readonly sessions = new Map<string, DrySession>();

  async start(input: WorkerStartInput): Promise<{ sessionId: string; branch: string | null; checkoutPath: string | null }> {
    const scripts: ScriptedAttempt[] =
      input.task.scriptedAttempts ?? input.task.outcomes.map((result) => ({ result, resultReason: null, tokens: zeroTokens(), handoff: null, decision: null }));
    const script = scripts.find((candidate) => candidate.tier === input.tier.name) ?? scripts[input.attempt - 1] ?? scripts[scripts.length - 1];
    if (!script) throw new Error(`dry-run task ${input.task.taskId} has no scripted attempt ${input.attempt}`);
    const sessionId = `dry-${input.task.taskId}-${input.attempt}`;
    const branch = `dry/${input.task.taskId}/${input.attempt}`;
    const checkoutPath = `dry-run:${sessionId}`;
    this.sessions.set(sessionId, {
      sessionId,
      task: input.task,
      attempt: input.attempt,
      tier: input.tier,
      ceilingNanos: input.ceilingNanos,
      script,
      branch,
      checkoutPath,
      stopped: false,
    });
    return { sessionId, branch, checkoutPath };
  }

  async wait(sessionId: string): Promise<WorkerResult> {
    const session = this.session(sessionId);
    if (session.script.result !== 'stopped' || session.ceilingNanos === null) return resultFor(session, 'idle');
    if (session.stopped) return resultFor(session, 'terminated');
    return new Promise((resolve) => {
      session.resolve = resolve;
    });
  }

  async usageFor(sessionId: string): Promise<LiveUsage | null> {
    const session = this.session(sessionId);
    const tokens = meteredTokens(session.script.tokens, session.tier, session.ceilingNanos, session.script.result);
    return { tokens, estimatedCostNanos: costNanos(tokens, session.tier.price) };
  }

  async stop(sessionId: string, _reason: string): Promise<void> {
    const session = this.session(sessionId);
    session.stopped = true;
    setTimeout(() => session.resolve?.(resultFor(session, 'terminated')), 0);
  }

  async verify(input: VerifyInput): Promise<VerifyResult> {
    const session = [...this.sessions.values()].find((candidate) => candidate.checkoutPath === input.checkoutPath || candidate.branch === input.branch);
    if (!session) return { passed: false, reason: 'dry-run session was not found' };
    if (session.script.result === 'passed') return { passed: true, reason: null };
    return { passed: false, reason: session.script.resultReason ?? `scripted ${session.script.result}` };
  }

  async summaryFor(sessionId: string): Promise<HandoffSummary | null> {
    const session = this.session(sessionId);
    const next = session.task.scriptedAttempts?.[session.attempt];
    const type = next?.handoff ?? 'entire-handoff';
    if (type === 'restart') return null;
    return {
      type,
      summary: `Dry-run handoff from ${session.task.taskId} attempt ${session.attempt}: ${session.script.resultReason ?? session.script.result}.`,
    };
  }

  private session(sessionId: string): DrySession {
    const session = this.sessions.get(sessionId);
    if (!session) throw new Error(`unknown dry-run session ${sessionId}`);
    return session;
  }
}

function resultFor(session: DrySession, status: WorkerResult['status']): WorkerResult {
  return { status, branch: session.branch, checkoutPath: session.checkoutPath, prUrl: null };

# ao session

Manage agent sessions: list, inspect, rename, kill, restore, exit or resume an
agent, switch harnesses, clean up, and claim PRs.

## In-app session links

When referring a user or another agent to a session in AO Chat or the AO
terminal, emit this canonical link:

```text
ao://sessions/{project-id}/{session-id}
```

- Use stable IDs returned by `ao project ls` and `ao session ls`, or the current
  session's `AO_PROJECT_ID` and `AO_SESSION_ID`. Never use display names as
  identity; renaming a session must not change its link.
- Treat the project ID and session ID as separate URL path segments. Encode
  either ID with URL percent encoding if it contains characters that are not
  safe in one segment.
- Emit only the navigation route above. Do not append query strings, fragments,
  action names, credentials, authorities, or extra path segments.
- The link is handled only inside a currently running AO desktop app. It is not
  an operating-system protocol link and must not be described as supporting
  cold launch or navigation from external applications.
- A session link navigates; it never sends a message, executes a command, or
  performs another action.

Example for project `mercury` and session `mer-3`:

```text

```

## Syntax

# ao send

Send a message to a running agent session. Use this to correct or direct a live agent mid-stream without killing and respawning it.

## Syntax

```
ao send [flags]
```

## Flags

| Flag | Meaning | Default / Required |
|---|---|---|
| `--message string` | Message body | Required unless `--recover-only` |
| `--session string` | Session id | Required |
| `--steer` | Add guidance to the active Chat turn, or start a normal turn when idle | Optional |
| `--client-message-id string` | Stable delivery handle for steering and safe retries | Generated automatically with `--steer` |
| `--recover-only` | Recover the outcome for an existing delivery handle without resending | Requires `--steer` and `--client-message-id` |

## Steering and recovery

`--steer` uses one atomic daemon operation. If the session has an active Chat
turn, the message is added to that turn. If the session is idle, the message
starts a normal Chat turn. The state cannot change between those decisions and
leave the message queued as a separate correction.

Every steering request has a client message id. Supply one explicitly when a
caller must retain the handle across retries:

```bash
ao send --session mer-3 --steer --client-message-id correction-42 --message "Focus only on the backend."
```

If the command reports an uncertain outcome or a transport failure, preserve
the delivery handle printed in the error. Recover the existing result without
contacting the provider again:

```bash
ao send --session mer-3 --steer --recover-only --client-message-id correction-42
```

Do not invent a new client message id after an uncertain result. Reusing the
original id lets the daemon return the durable steering receipt or normal turn
without delivering the message twice. Recovery confirms the recorded delivery
outcome, not that the agent acted on the guidance.

## Examples

```bash
# Send a correction to a running session
ao send --session mer-3 --message "Focus only on the backend; ignore frontend files."
```

```bash
# Give the agent new instructions mid-task
ao send --session mer-3 --message "The issue is in session_manager.go line 142, not in the CLI. Investigate there."
```

```bash
# Steer the active Chat turn, or start a normal turn if it is idle
ao send --session mer-3 --steer --message "Use the daemon DTO as the source of truth."
```

import { costNanos } from '../schema/money.js';
import type { TallyConfig, TaskSize, Tier, TokenUsage } from '../schema/types.js';
import { PriceHistory } from '../agent/history.js';
import type { HandoffSummary, LiveUsage, LiveUsagePort, SessionControlPort, SizingSignals, SizingSignalsPort } from '../agent/ports.js';
import type { VerifierPort, VerifyInput, VerifyResult } from '../adapters/verifier.js';
import { type BacklogTask, loadFileBacklog, type ScriptedAttempt } from './backlog.js';
import type { RealRunPorts, WorkerPort, WorkerResult, WorkerStartInput } from './real.js';

interface DrySession {
  sessionId: string;
  task: BacklogTask;
  attempt: number;
  tier: Tier;
  ceilingNanos: number | null;
  script: ScriptedAttempt;
  branch: string;
  checkoutPath: string;
  stopped: boolean;
  resolve?: (result: WorkerResult) => void;
}

class DryRunState implements WorkerPort, LiveUsagePort, SessionControlPort, VerifierPort {
  private readonly sessions = new Map<string, DrySession>();

  async start(input: WorkerStartInput): Promise<{ sessionId: string; branch: string | null; checkoutPath: string | null }> {
    const scripts: ScriptedAttempt[] =
      input.task.scriptedAttempts ?? input.task.outcomes.map((result) => ({ result, resultReason: null, tokens: zeroTokens(), handoff: null, decision: null }));
    const script = scripts.find((candidate) => candidate.tier === input.tier.name) ?? scripts[input.attempt - 1] ?? scripts[scripts.length - 1];
    if (!script) throw new Error(`dry-run task ${input.task.taskId} has no scripted attempt ${input.attempt}`);
    const sessionId = `dry-${input.task.taskId}-${input.attempt}`;
    const branch = `dry/${input.task.taskId}/${input.attempt}`;
    const checkoutPath = `dry-run:${sessionId}`;
    this.sessions.set(sessionId, {
      sessionId,
      task: input.task,
      attempt: input.attempt,
      tier: input.tier,
      ceilingNanos: input.ceilingNanos,
      script,
      branch,
      checkoutPath,
      stopped: false,
    });
    return { sessionId, branch, checkoutPath };
  }

  async wait(sessionId: string): Promise<WorkerResult> {
    const session = this.session(sessionId);
    if (session.script.result !== 'stopped' || session.ceilingNanos === null) return resultFor(session, 'idle');
    if (session.stopped) return resultFor(session, 'terminated');
    return new Promise((resolve) => {
      session.resolve = resolve;
    });
  }

  async usageFor(sessionId: string): Promise<LiveUsage | null> {
    const session = this.session(sessionId);
    const tokens = meteredTokens(session.script.tokens, session.tier, session.ceilingNanos, session.script.result);
    return { tokens, estimatedCostNanos: costNanos(tokens, session.tier.price) };
  }

  async stop(sessionId: string, _reason: string): Promise<void> {
    const session = this.session(sessionId);
    session.stopped = true;
    setTimeout(() => session.resolve?.(resultFor(session, 'terminated')), 0);
  }

  async verify(input: VerifyInput): Promise<VerifyResult> {
    const session = [...this.sessions.values()].find((candidate) => candidate.checkoutPath === input.checkoutPath || candidate.branch === input.branch);
    if (!session) return { passed: false, reason: 'dry-run session was not found' };
    if (session.script.result === 'passed') return { passed: true, reason: null };
    return { passed: false, reason: session.script.resultReason ?? `scripted ${session.script.result}` };
  }

  async summaryFor(sessionId: string): Promise<HandoffSummary | null> {
    const session = this.session(sessionId);
    const next = session.task.scriptedAttempts?.[session.attempt];
    const type = next?.handoff ?? 'entire-handoff';
    if (type === 'restart') return null;
    return {
      type,
      summary: `Dry-run handoff from ${session.task.taskId} attempt ${session.attempt}: ${session.script.resultReason ?? session.script.result}.`,
    };
  }

  private session(sessionId: string): DrySession {
    const session = this.sessions.get(sessionId);
    if (!session) throw new Error(`unknown dry-run session ${sessionId}`);
    return session;
  }
}

function resultFor(session: DrySession, status: WorkerResult['status']): WorkerResult {
  return { status, branch: session.branch, checkoutPath: session.checkoutPath, prUrl: null };
"}

# Graph view (PR #55): review 1, changes requested

Reviewed by the orchestrator on 11 Oct from the PR merged with main, using the fixture replay, in headless Chrome at 1440 px and 390 px with every graph opened. Screenshots: `graph-desktop.png` and `graph-phone.png` in this folder.

## What works

- It belongs to the page: same paper, type and line language; red only on the stopped attempt and the outside-slice edit.
- The small cases (G1, G2) read in a few seconds. The caption, the attempt line and "Edited outside predicted slice" are clear.
- Three-column layout on desktop (callers, targets, related) is the right idea.

## Must fix before merge

1. **The large case is a wall, not a picture.** G3 draws 40 near-identical boxes in a column several screens tall. Nobody reads that in five seconds. Group by kind and summarise: show the targets in full, then at most a handful of the highest-weight callers, co-change files and tests each, followed by one quiet "+31 more callers" line per group. The caption already carries the totals. A graph should never be taller than about one screen on desktop.
2. **Labels collapse to the same text.** Every caller in G3 shortens to `src/services/servi.../ledger_adapter.py`, so the nodes are indistinguishable. Shorten so the part that differs survives (keep the distinguishing directory, drop the common prefix), and when siblings share a prefix, state the prefix once.
3. **Edges in the large case are noise.** The fan from the target crosses behind every box, and the test column has zigzag segments between boxes. With grouping this mostly goes away; where edges remain they must not run under other nodes.
4. **Phone width overflows.** At 390 px the caption is cut off at the right ("tests present → mediu"), node boxes run past the right edge, and each task row leaves a tall empty block beside the red rule before the graph. Nothing may be clipped or need sideways scrolling; the vertical stack needs the same grouping and "+N more" treatment.
5. **The "Why" column is squeezed to one word per line on desktop** (see task 2: "Latest / attempt / continues / the / previous / work."). Whether or not this PR caused it, the task table must give the reason a readable measure; this is the sentence the demo is built on.
6. Small: "1 files" should be "1 file" everywhere (row summary and "1 files edited").

## Check after fixing

- Same three fixture tasks at 1440 px and 390 px, graphs open, plus a 6-node and a 15-node case so the grouping threshold is seen.
- No horizontal overflow at 390 px (check `document.documentElement.scrollWidth` equals the viewport width).
- Replay still updates in place with no layout jump when a group count changes.
